topic: Banica–Özteke–Pittau's prime Fourier truncation isolation conjecture
title: Extending Banica–Özteke–Pittau's Fourier defect theory: a correction to their truncation conjecture

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Banica–Özteke–Pittau's Fourier defect theory, we refute their Conjecture 1.14 (Isolated partial Hadamard matrices, and related topics, arXiv:1706.00986v2, p. 9): Fourier incidence equations and the analytic implicit-function theorem give non-isolation after any two row deletions at every prime order p ≥ 5. For any nonempty proper row set of size m, the local dephased solution space is a real-analytic manifold of dimension (m−1)(p−m−1). Thus among the nonempty prime Fourier truncations, precisely those with m = 1, p−1, p are isolated, and no fixed positive density margin ensures isolation. We also give an explicit defect formula for every row truncation of a finite abelian Fourier matrix; its zero-cycle case has the same analytic dimension formula with p replaced by the group order.
summary: A proper m-row prime Fourier truncation has local dephased dimension (m−1)(p−m−1), so the nonempty isolated cases are exactly m = 1, p−1, p. For a finite abelian group of order N, the undephased defect is m(N−m+1) plus the total number of retained nontrivial cyclic cosets, counted once for each nonzero step. The zero-cycle case is an analytic regular level set; singular cases have only a tangent-dimension conclusion.
